kinds.d: Lithium aluminium pyroxene specimen: pale prisms and the gem varieties kunzite and hiddenite; also the main lithium ore.

x.d: Pink to lilac spodumene coloured by manganese, discovered in 1902 and named for George F. Kunz of Tiffany & Co.; fades in sunlight.
Emerald-green chromium-bearing spodumene first reported at Hiddenite, Alexander County, North Carolina; named for William Earl Hidden.
Yellowish spodumene.
Single crystals reported up to 14.3 m in the Black Hills of South Dakota.
Type-locality spodumene from Utö, Sweden, first described in 1800 by José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva.

kinds.d: Calcium magnesium pyroxene specimen: green prismatic crystals; chrome diopside and star diopside are gem forms.

x.d: Deep green diopside coloured by chromium, sometimes called Siberian emerald.
Manganese-rich violet to light blue diopside.
Black diopside cut to show a four-ray star.
Diopside crystals from Ala, Piedmont, and St Marcel, Val d'Aosta.
Diopside from Schwarzenstein, Zillertal, Tirol.
Chromian diopside from Outokumpu, Finland.

kinds.d: Sodium aluminium pyroxene specimen: the rock jade in white, green and lavender; imperial jade is the emerald-green grade.

x.d: The most valuable jadeite, an intense emerald green from chromium.
Pale violet jadeite, for example from Bursa Province, Turkey.
Very dark green to black jadeite.
Northern Myanmar, source of most gem-quality jadeite.
Jadeite from the Motagua Valley, Guatemala.
Jadeite from Itoigawa and the Ohmi area, Niigata, Japan; Neolithic beads and axes were made from it.
Experimental synthesis began in the early 1950s; GE and others produced it for research in the 1980s.

kinds.d: Manganese silicate specimen: rose-pink masses veined with black manganese oxide, used as an ornamental stone.

x.d: Pink rhodonite from near Yekaterinburg, the main 19th-century ornamental source; a block was used for the Tomb of Tsarina Maria Alexandrovna, completed 1906.
Rhodonite from Långban and Pajsberg near Filipstad, Sweden.
Rhodonite from Franklin Furnace, New Jersey.
Gem rhodonite crystals from Broken Hill, New South Wales.
Rhodonite from the Serrana mine, El Molar, Tarragona.

kinds.d: Calcium magnesium iron amphibole specimen: green fibrous or bladed crystals; nephrite jade and cat's-eye are gem forms.

x.d: Compact fibrous actinolite-tremolite that is one of the two jades.
Chatoyant green to yellowish-green actinolite.
Actinolite from Mt Greiner, Zillertal, and Untersulzbachtal.
Taiwan and Canada are named as major gem sources.

kinds.d: Calcium magnesium amphibole specimen: white to grey blades; nephrite jade and asbestiform tremolite are forms.

x.d: Green crystalline variety of tremolite, one of the two jades.
Type-locality tremolite from Campolungo, Piumogna Valley, Ticino, first described in 1789.
Fibrous tremolite, one of six recognised asbestos types; handle with care.
Tremolite from the Brumado mine, Bahia, Brazil.
Tremolite from Pierrepont, Gouverneur, Edwards and Macomb, St Lawrence County, New York.

kinds.d: Sodium manganese silicate hydroxide specimen: salmon-pink to orange crystals, the manganese counterpart of pectolite.

x.d: Pink to orange serandite crystals from Mont Saint-Hilaire, Quebec.
x.dt: crystals on matrix · thumbnail to miniature

x.d: Serandite from Rouma Island, Los Islands, Guinea.
Described in 1931 by Lacroix and named for mineral collector J. M. Sérand.

kinds.d: Potassium sodium lithium iron titanium silicate specimen: black prisms, notably with benitoite in San Benito County.

x.d: Splendid neptunite crystals from the Gem mine and Mina Numero Uno, San Benito County, California, in natrolite veins.
x.dt: black prisms on natrolite · thumbnail to miniature

x.d: Type-locality neptunite from Narssârssuk, Greenland, first described in 1893.
Neptunite from Mont Saint-Hilaire, Quebec.
Neptunite from the Khibiny and Lovozero massifs.

kinds.d: Calcium iron silicate hydroxide specimen: black glassy prisms in basalt cavities, named for William Babington.

x.d: Exceptional babingtonite crystals from Lane's quarry, Westfield, Massachusetts.
x.dt: black crystals on datolite or prehnite

x.d: Type-locality babingtonite from Arendal, Norway, first described in 1824.
Babingtonite from the Khandivali quarry near Mumbai.
Babingtonite from Qiaojia, Yunnan, China.

notes: All 9 planned kinds kept. HOM has no serandite file; Wikipedia used. Sources: Wikipedia plus HOM for the other eight. Not on fetched pages and omitted: Inagli/Yakutia diopside, Maw sit sit jade, Pala kunzite. No brands or traditions.
